name: KY-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+20 partisan lean in a heavily Republican district
Incumbent Brett Guthrie seeking re-election with a large financial edge
Democrat Megan Wingfield has raised only about $7,500
model.rationale: The district's R+20 lean, Guthrie's incumbency and roughly 600-to-1 fundraising advantage leave no evidence pointing toward an upset, and markets agree at about 95% Republican. The forecast stays essentially at the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: A major late outside spending push for Wingfield or a scandal involving Guthrie would be the only plausible route to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Kentucky's 2nd District is a deeply Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about R+20, and Brett Guthrie is a well-established incumbent seeking another term. He has raised more than $4.7 million and holds $1.7 million on hand, while Democratic nominee Megan Wingfield has raised under $8,000 and reported just $1,197 in cash. No outside groups are spending against Guthrie, and no expert race raters list the contest, treating it as safely Republican.

Prediction markets give Guthrie roughly a 95% chance of winning, consistent with the district's fundamentals. There are no public general-election polls, so the forecast rests on the partisan baseline, incumbency and the lopsided money picture. Barring an extraordinary development, Guthrie is positioned to win comfortably.
